name: Single-Leg Machine Leg Extension
description: The single-leg machine leg extension trains one quadriceps at a time using the leg extension machine, with the non-working leg hanging free. Training unilaterally ensures equal development of both legs and allows greater focus on the mind-muscle connection. It is particularly useful during rehabilitation after knee injuries when the injured limb requires specific, isolated strengthening.

execution.starting_position: Sit on the leg extension machine. Place one leg under the pad with the knee at approximately 90 degrees. The other leg is free and not on the pad.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust the seat and pad to fit one leg. Set an appropriate weight — use less than the bilateral version.
steps: Step 1: Grip the handles and brace lightly.
Step 2: Extend the working knee to bring the leg to full extension.
Step 3: Squeeze the quadriceps at the top of the movement.
Step 4: Lower with control back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on extension, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Using momentum to swing the weight
safety_considerations: Very high patellar load — use controlled tempo and appropriate weight
If you have patellar issues, limit range to pain-free only
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at the top. Return to 90 degrees of flexion at the bottom.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2-1-3-0 (slow eccentric is especially valuable for quad development)
coaching_cues: Squeeze the quad at the top
